issues.legal_issue: The special limitation rule governs a successor manager’s suit to recover endowed property transferred by a previous manager for valuable consideration, regardless of whether the transferor represented the property as his own.
material_facts: The properties were found to belong to a temple and had been transferred by previous managers for valuable consideration.
The transfer documents represented that the properties belonged to the transferors as their separate property.
issues.conclusion: The special limitation rule applied because the properties belonged to the endowment, were transferred by previous managers, and the transfers were for valuable consideration; the transferors’ representations about ownership did not alter that result.
issues.legal_principle: Article 134-B of the Limitation Act, 1908 applies when the property is comprised in a Hindu religious or charitable endowment, was transferred by a previous manager, and the transfer was for valuable consideration. The character of the transferor’s representations about the property is irrelevant. The Court applied Mahant Sudarsan Das v. Mahant Ram Kirpal Das in reading the article according to its text, and distinguished execution sales from transfers made by a previous manager.

rule.if: suit_by_successor_manager_to_recover_endowment_property and property_belongs_to_endowment and transferred_by_previous_manager and transfer_for_valuable_consideration

predicates.suit_by_successor_manager_to_recover_end: A successor manager brings a suit to recover property said to belong to a religious or charitable endowment.
predicates.property_belongs_to_endowment: The property is found to be comprised in a religious or charitable endowment.
predicates.transferred_by_previous_manager: A previous manager transferred the property.
predicates.transfer_for_valuable_consideration: The previous manager transferred the property for valuable consideration.
predicates.special_limitation_rule_applies_regardle: The special limitation rule governs the recovery suit even if the transferor represented that the property belonged to him personally.

issues.definition: When a successor manager sues to recover endowed property transferred by a previous manager for valuable consideration, the special limitation rule applies even if the transferor claimed personal ownership.

issues.legal_issue: A transferee acquires prescriptive title against an endowment when the transferring manager has been removed from management and the limitation period for recovery has elapsed before the trustees seek possession.
material_facts: The transferor disposed of the temple properties, left the village, and ceased taking part in temple management.
Other persons performed worship and acted as de facto managers for more than the limitation period before the suit was brought.

The trustees were appointed after that period had elapsed and sought possession, but the transferees brought a suit for declaration of title and an injunction before the possession order was executed.
issues.conclusion: The evidence showed that the transferor had been removed from management and that the limitation period had elapsed from that removal. A recovery suit by the trustees would therefore have been barred, so the transferees’ prescriptive title was upheld and the trial and lower appellate decrees were restored.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 134-B of the Limitation Act, 1908, time for a successor manager’s suit to recover endowed property transferred by a previous manager runs from the transferor’s death, resignation, or removal. Removal may be established by evidence that the transferor abandoned management and other persons took over as de facto managers. Once the limitation period has elapsed from removal, the later trustees’ recovery claim is barred.

rule.if: appeal_in_title_and_injunction_suit and property_belongs_to_endowment and transferred_by_previous_manager and transferor_abandoned_management and other_persons_assumed_de_facto_management and limitation_period_elapsed_after_removal

predicates.appeal_in_title_and_injunction_suit: The proceeding is an appeal arising from a suit seeking a declaration of title and an injunction against interference with possession.
predicates.property_belongs_to_endowment: The property is found to be comprised in a religious or charitable endowment.
predicates.transferred_by_previous_manager: A previous manager transferred the property.
predicates.transferor_abandoned_management: The transferor left management and ceased taking part in the affairs of the endowment.
predicates.other_persons_assumed_de_facto_managemen: Other persons took over the management of the endowment in practice.
predicates.limitation_period_elapsed_after_removal: The applicable limitation period for recovery elapsed after the transferor’s removal from management and before the trustees sought possession.
predicates.transferee_prescriptive_title_defeats_la: The transferee’s prescriptive title prevents the later trustees from recovering the property.

issues.definition: In an appeal from a title-and-injunction suit, where endowed property was transferred by a previous manager who abandoned management, other persons took over in practice, and the limitation period elapsed after removal, the transferee’s prescriptive title defeats the later recovery claim.
